provider: Google Drive shared drives written by service accounts (the SA chain, corrected)

free_tier.stated: Service accounts now report storageQuota limit '0' — they cannot own files at all. Real quota comes from the parent tenant: Education/Nonprofit 100 TB pooled, Business Standard 2 TB x users, Business Plus 5 TB x users. The '15 GB per SA x 100 SA x 30 projects = 45 TB' claim in the reference repo is DEAD.

egress.terms: No per-GB egress charge for Drive file downloads; drive.usercontent.google.com serves direct bytes. New ceiling: Drive API 1 TB/day per project egress.

tooling: rclone drive backend with service_account_file + shared drive config (rclone docs still document the SA + shared-drive path and warn its shared client_id is being retired during 2026 — make your own). gclone (156 stars, archived), AutoRcloneV2, 88lex/sa-gen (71 stars, last push 2023-05) automate SA creation but not the new shared-drive target.
chaining: The chain inverted. Old: unlimited free SAs x 15 GB each. New: SAs are free and unlimited but hold zero bytes, so they become pure WRITE THROUGHPUT/multiplexer against one tenant's pooled shared drive. 750 GB/day is per acting identity, and each SA is a distinct identity, so N SAs lifting into one shared drive gives N x 750 GB/day ingest; the 100 TB pool is the actual ceiling.
limits_note: SA quota limit = 0 (hard); shared drive 500,000 items / 100 nesting levels; 750 GB/day upload per user; 5 TB max file; Drive API 400,000,000 quota units/day/project before charges and a 1 TB/day egress cap; 1,000,000 units/min/project.

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: g levels; 750 GB/day upload per user; 5 TB max file; Drive API 400,000,000 quota units/day/project before charges and a 1 TB/day egress cap; 1,000,000 units/min/project. cloud-drive

reliability_note: The widely-copied 45 TB recipe now returns 403 storageQuotaExceeded on every upload; every SA-based rclone tutorial written before ~2024 is wrong unless it targets a shared drive. Also reported: a hard ~16 GB SA limit when uploading into a *My Drive* folder shared with the SA (2024 SO thread) — shared drives are the only working target.
